tasks.task: Run a security health check and build the risk register

items.when: When an owner answers a question set and needs gaps scored in plain words and a register
When you need to know which basic safeguards come first for this size of business
When a customer or insurer expects the check set out against a known framework
When a fix is proposed, to ask what it protects, what it costs and what it still assumes
When the report is drafted, to have a fresh reviewer read it as a non-technical owner

tasks.task: Write the first 90-day security plan

items.when: For a new client with no plan, after a near miss, or when an insurer asks what is in place
When the budget is tight, to compare a bare-minimum plan with a fuller one, with money and dates
When the order of fixes is unclear, to see which safeguards to do first
Before handing over, to check the owner can see what to do each week and why

tasks.task: Write staff security rules on one page

items.when: When every member of staff needs one page of plain rules for the handbook or the wall
When the rules must cover passwords and second-step sign-in for staff and customers
When staff paste work into AI tools and need rules on what may and may not go in
When people work from home or on their own devices and the rules must say how
When the rules are approved and need a plain explanation and a staff announcement
When staff ignore a rule, to ask what makes it hard to follow and fix that

tasks.task: Build a phishing and payment-fraud awareness session

items.when: When a small team needs a 30-minute session with made-up examples from their own sector
When 30 minutes is too long, to try a one-page rule sheet with a ten-minute drill
When people need one page to keep at their desk a month after the session
A week later, to test what stuck with a short quiz at three levels
Some weeks later, to see if staff follow the call-back rule and what gets in the way

tasks.task: Check a suspicious message or payment request

items.when: When someone got a message asking for a payment, a bank change, a code, a sign-in or a file
When someone already clicked or replied, to set severity, who to tell and what to keep
When money may have moved, to trace the flow in the records and list what to check next
When a breach notice or scare arrives, to separate what is known from what is feared

tasks.task: Write the what-to-do-if-hit plan

items.when: When the business needs one page on who decides, who to call, first steps and what to save
When one system matters most and needs its own steps, severity levels and who to tell
When the plan must say how much loss is bearable and how systems come back
When the plan is drafted, to test its contain and recover steps against a likely attack
When the plan assumes calm people, to check handoffs, warnings and human mistakes

tasks.task: Rehearse the plan with a tabletop exercise

items.when: When there is a plan or a draft and the team can give under an hour, with no live system touched
Before the exercise, to have the plan the team will be tested against
When one scenario is too easy, to model several things going wrong at once
After the exercise, to turn what went wrong into changes with owners and dates

tasks.task: Handle a live incident and tell the people affected

items.when: In the first minutes, to set severity, who to tell, what to preserve and the next steps
When several people are working the incident and need roles, evidence rules and recovery checks
When customers or staff must be told, to state what happened, the facts and the next step
When writing to those affected, to start with them, state known facts and name owners
Before any notice goes out, to check each statement against what the logs really show

tasks.task: Lock down a store's logins, staff access and settings

items.when: When a small online store needs its admin, staff access and checkout tightened
When you need a ranked fix list and a score from the admin team and app list
When you want one run to a fix list, a sign-in policy and a phishing rule sheet
When sign-in is the worry, to rank the gaps and set a password and second-step policy
When payment and checkout settings may be loose, to score them and rank the fixes

tasks.task: Stop a card-testing attack in the first hour

items.when: When a store shows many small orders, declined payments or odd names, often at night
After the first hour, to set fraud rules, a review routine and a bot access plan
When bots drive the attack, to decide which to allow, check or block at login and checkout
When orders from the attack window must be reviewed by risk level before shipping

tasks.task: Set fraud rules and a review routine for orders

items.when: When fake orders are part of a wider store lockdown and the rules must fit it
When you have order volume and payment set-up and need rules and a chargeback watch line
When you want a second set of rules by risk level to compare with the first
When a dispute arrives, to see what proof to collect or whether to accept it
After a month, to see if fraud cancellations fell and good orders were not blocked

tasks.task: Review risky apps and scripts on a store or site

items.when: When the app list has grown, to mark each keep, swap or cut and rank the scripts left
When you need each script and package scored for risk and what to remove
When one app handles customer data, to tier its risk and ask it the right questions

tasks.task: Check a website for basic security gaps

items.when: When the owner wants a baseline check of HTTPS, headers and secrets with ranked fixes
When keys or private files may be readable by visitors on a site the client owns
When a key has leaked, to find the rest, rotate them and check the live site
When the site is a custom app the client owns, to check for common web flaws
When the site is WordPress, to turn its health report into a backup-first fix plan

tasks.task: Protect the email domain from spoofing

items.when: When you have the DNS records, to score the set-up and get the exact fixes
When sender records are missing, to set them up without sending real mail to spam
When domains have piled up, to flag leftover records and weak registrar access

tasks.task: Plan backups and rehearse a restore

items.when: When nobody knows how much data loss is bearable or how a restore would run
When backups exist but were never tested, to plan a safe restore test and an evidence log
After the test, to compare the evidence with the recovery targets and assign open gaps

tasks.task: Review access and remove leavers

items.when: When accounts have piled up, to find old logins, inactive users and too much access
When someone leaves, to get a checklist that covers accounts, devices and handover
Before a role or system change, to review who can reach staff or customer data
When the office runs on Microsoft 365 and the fixes are user, mail and security settings

tasks.task: Turn notes into a risk register

items.when: When you have notes from a meeting, an audit, an insurer's form or an incident
When the notes describe a system, to find threats, rate them and add a way to reduce each
When the register must use the same scoring words the owner agreed in the health check

tasks.task: Run the quarterly security review

items.when: Every three months, with about an hour of the owner's time and a few exports
When the client is a store, to score against last quarter and pick the fixes to do first
Each quarter, to recheck who still has access and who should not

tasks.task: Answer an insurer's or customer's security questionnaire

items.when: When a questionnaire arrives, to draft sourced answers and an evidence index
When the form is long, to sort the must-haves and see where the business falls short
When the form is for cover, to list the risks, the usual cover and questions for the broker
Before sending, to tie every yes to a setting, a policy or a record, or change the answer

tasks.task: Check the business against a security standard

items.when: When the client wants UK Cyber Essentials, to find gaps before applying
When a customer asks for a NIST CSF view of where the business is and where it is going
When the business takes cards, to find its PCI level and the right self-check form
When the client may fall under the EU network security rules and their reporting deadlines

tasks.task: Vet a new tool or vendor before staff use it

items.when: When a tool will hold company or customer data, to tier the risk and question the vendor
When the tool is an AI service, to flag data-training, liability and model-change terms
When the tool is sold as making things safer, to ask what it changes and what it costs

always.when: Before any plan, rule sheet or notice goes out, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the fixes are device, account, licence or network settings someone must apply
When the job needs privacy records, a breach duty check or audit evidence
When the client builds its own app and needs code review or a threat model
When store fixes mean changing theme, checkout or app settings in Shopify
When a WordPress or WooCommerce site needs plugins removed, updated or hardened
When an incident needs customer, press and staff messages written and timed

gaps: No library item checks one suspicious email, text or call for fraud signs; only the kit prompt does
No library item plans a password manager and two-step sign-in rollout for an office that is not a store
No library item covers device basics: updates, disk encryption, screen lock and a lost or stolen laptop
No library item gives a ransomware playbook for a small business
No library item walks through recovering a hacked email, social or store account
No library item writes a breach notice to customers or decides who must be told and by when
No library item writes a tabletop exercise script with timed surprises; only the kit prompt does
No library item sets a call-back rule and steps for bank-detail changes and urgent payment requests
No library item checks office or home Wi-Fi and router settings
No library item locks down a WooCommerce store; the store security items are written for Shopify
No library item makes clearly different awareness session formats to compare
